hints.title: Adjacent Exclusion Branching Obstacle
hints.text: Robbing two adjacent houses triggers an alarm. At each house, you must choose between robbing it and adding its loot to the best total from two houses back, or skipping it to keep the best total from the previous house. How can you track this choice without re-evaluating earlier houses?

hints.title: Non-Adjacent Optimal Substructure Invariant
hints.text: The maximum loot up to house i is the greater of skipping house i or robbing house i plus the maximum loot up to house i-2.

hints.title: Two-State Rolling Maximization Procedure
hints.text: Maintain two running values: the maximum loot achieved two houses back and one house back. For each house's value, compute the new maximum as the greater of the previous house's total or the two-back total plus current value. Shift the running values forward and return the final total.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Single pass over nums updating two running values.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all valid non-consecutive subsets explores 2^N combinations, timing out on arrays with over 30 elements.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining rob1 and rob2 avoids allocating an O(N) array while retaining O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Formulating max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]) and reducing space to two scalar variables.
